svg.aria-label: How to write olá: 3 letters, o, l, á, one after another
svg.title: Writing olá
svg.desc: 3 letters written one after another: o, l, á (latin). Each letter has its own group of frames; frame N of a group shows movements 1 to N of that letter, the movement being added drawn in ink over the finished letter, whose outline is read from _fonts/LatinPrint-Subset.ttf. Each letter is drawn at its own scale from its own cited stroke order, so the strip does not show how large the letters are next to each other, how far apart they sit, or any join between them. Stroke order: o: Grundschrift-App (Laborschule Bielefeld, Bielefeld University, with the Grundschulverband), level kleinbuchstaben/o, ordered stroke paths for o (assets/levels/kleinbuchstaben/o/metadata.json, commit f6dbd80; no licence, facts only) <https://github.com/Medien-Treibhaus/grundschrift-app-source/blob/f6dbd807adbb3fc2f94207fe578def439f6e9c49/assets/levels/kleinbuchstaben/o/metadata.json>; l: Grundschrift-App (Laborschule Bielefeld, Bielefeld University, with the Grundschulverband), level kleinbuchstaben/l, ordered stroke paths for l (assets/levels/kleinbuchstaben/l/metadata.json, commit f6dbd80; no licence, facts only) <https://github.com/Medien-Treibhaus/grundschrift-app-source/blob/f6dbd807adbb3fc2f94207fe578def439f6e9c49/assets/levels/kleinbuchstaben/l/metadata.json>; á: UJIpenchars2 (F. Prat, M. J. Castro, D. Llorens, A. Marzal and J. M. Vilar), UCI Machine Learning Repository dataset 177, class á: 120 tablet pen traces by 60 native Spanish writers (CC BY 4.0); the a after the Grundschrift-App, level kleinbuchstaben/a (commit f6dbd80) <https://archive.ics.uci.edu/dataset/177/uji+pen+characters+version+2>. Source notes on variation: o: The Grundschrift-App was made in a research project of the Laborschule at Bielefeld University with the Grundschulverband, on its Grundschrift school model, with a teacher advisory team. Each letter is an ordered list of paths, one per pen-down stroke, which the app makes a child trace in order. It writes o in one stroke, from the top, anticlockwise, all the way round. UJIpenchars2 (Prat, Castro, Llorens, Marzal and Vilar; UCI Machine Learning Repository dataset 177, CC BY 4.0) holds 120 tablet pen traces of o, two by each of 60 adult Spanish writers; only counts are cited. All 120 are one stroke; 62 start at the top centre (24 top left, 23 top right), and 118 turn anticlockwise. The app's repository has no licence, so only the order, the start, the direction and the lifts are taken from it; no point is copied, and the path is fitted to the o of the bundled LatinPrint-Subset.ttf, a renamed subset of SIL Global's literacy typeface Andika 7.000, which prints the one-storey a the school model teaches; the book's own text face is a different font. Handwriting varies by writer. l: The Grundschrift-App was made in a research project of the Laborschule at Bielefeld University with the Grundschulverband, on its Grundschrift school model, with a teacher advisory team. Each letter is an ordered list of paths, one per pen-down stroke, which the app makes a child trace in order. It writes l in one stroke, down from the top. Grundschrift ends the stroke with a small hook to the right that the bundled outline does not print, so the path ends where the printed letter ends. UJIpenchars2 (Prat, Castro, Llorens, Marzal and Vilar; UCI Machine Learning Repository dataset 177, CC BY 4.0) holds 120 tablet pen traces of l, two by each of 60 adult Spanish writers; only counts are cited. All 120 are one stroke, the source's count, but 93 of them start at the bottom left and loop up, as a joined hand does; 9 start at the top left, as the school model does. The app's repository has no licence, so only the order, the start, the direction and the lifts are taken from it; no point is copied, and the path is fitted to the l of the bundled LatinPrint-Subset.ttf, a renamed subset of SIL Global's literacy typeface Andika 7.000, which prints the one-storey a the school model teaches; the book's own text face is a different font. Handwriting varies by writer. á: UJIpenchars2 (Prat, Castro, Llorens, Marzal and Vilar; UCI Machine Learning Repository dataset 177, CC BY 4.0) holds 120 tablet pen traces of á, two by each of 60 adult Spanish writers; only counts are cited. All 120 are two strokes; the accent is found as a separate mark above the letter in all 120 and drawn last in all 120. Its direction splits: 74 draw it up to the right, 40 down to the left. The a is the Grundschrift-App's a (level kleinbuchstaben/a, commit f6dbd80; no licence, facts only). The accent is drawn up to the right, as most of these writers draw it; about three in ten draw it down to the left. Only counts and shares are cited; no trace is copied, and the path is fitted to the á of the bundled LatinPrint-Subset.ttf, a renamed subset of SIL Global's literacy typeface Andika 7.000, which prints the one-storey a the school model teaches; the book's own text face is a different font. Handwriting varies by writer.
svg.text: How it is written — 3 letters, one after another
Letter 3 of 3 — 2 strokes · 1 pen lift · 3 movements
Letter 1: stroke order after Grundschrift-App (Laborschule Bielefeld, Bielefeld University, with the Grundschulverband), level kleinbuchstaben/o, ordered
stroke paths for o (assets/levels/kleinbuchstaben/o/metadata.json, commit f6dbd80; no licence, facts only)
Letter 2: stroke order after Grundschrift-App (Laborschule Bielefeld, Bielefeld University, with the Grundschulverband), level kleinbuchstaben/l, ordered
stroke paths for l (assets/levels/kleinbuchstaben/l/metadata.json, commit f6dbd80; no licence, facts only)
Letter 3: stroke order after UJIpenchars2 (F. Prat, M. J. Castro, D. Llorens, A. Marzal and J. M. Vilar), UCI Machine Learning Repository dataset 177, class
á: 120 tablet pen traces by 60 native Spanish writers (CC BY 4.0); the a after the Grundschrift-App, level kleinbuchstaben/a (commit f6dbd80)
This order is attested, not standardised; the source records where it varies.
